notes.title: Some Holiday Minigame Fixes and An Update on State of Cloud Saving 12/23/2024
notes.content:
Hello all!

There have been a couple little updates we've been meaning to get around to and some things that we've looked into that we wanted to talk about before for the end of the holiday season as a lot of people have a little more time to invest in playing games during this time and/or may be starting our game to help with their new years resolutions.

[b]Updates[/b]
The gameplay changes mainly involve updating some of the arcade minigames to be a little less difficult, especially at the start of the game. We also finally removed the "Feedback" button from the main menu because we're well out of Early Access and I try to keep my eye out for issues in the Steam forums anyways.

[b]About Cloud Saving[/b]
As an update into one of the larger issues brought up in feedback/reviews, we've done a deep dive into what it would take to get cloud saving working for this game and it would be... a lot. 

Not only would we have to completely change the way saving works for the game (and the file type being saved), but we realized that it would undoubtedly erase all players current save data. If there were a way of doing so without putting player's data at risk, we would definitely go through with it, but it just seems too unfeasible. 

I'm very sorry. 

It happened because of our naivety in game development and is something we will take with us in the future as a lesson.

[b]Reviews[/b]
On a slightly lighter note, we are SO CLOSE to 10 reviews (which is a big deal for games on Steam) so if you've played it or are planning on playing it soon, please consider leaving a review, which will give our game a little better visibility on this platform (steam considers games with less than 10 reviews kind of lesser unfortunately).

We would really appreciate it and players coming in looking to see what the game is like based on your experience would benefit from an unbiased viewpoint.

[b]To Conclude[/b]
I want to thank everyone who's bought and played our little game, leaving feedback good and bad, and helped us make the game as good as we could this past year! We hope you all have a great Holiday season! And don't forget to get some KFC! ;)

ありがとう ございます!

-Zach

notes.title: Leaving Early Access and going into "Full Release"!
notes.content:
Hello! 

It's true, we are leaving Early Access! We received a lot of great feedback from players during our time in Early Access, and did what we could to address issues, add functionality, add content, and are confident and proud of what we were able to accomplish as a small 2 person team.

This is the last big update taking us from our time in Early Access into full release, where we are only going to be focusing on fixing any technical issues that come up. Because of this, we will leave the feedback form button in the main menu for a little longer in case any buggies are found.

Finally, here is a list of the updates that represent v1.0 of Kagami: An Odyssey in Japanese Language Learning!

[b]Features:[/b]
[list]
[*] Replaced the TTS voice for Kana, Vocab, and Phrases with Audio recorded by Japanese voice-over artist Ko Takehiro.
[*] Added a new minigame that goes over the first 55 core vocab accessible early in the game
[*] Added a new NPC that covers a little bit of grammar
[/list]

[b]Smaller Fixes/Changes:[/b]
[list]
[*] Switched out Hotel Audio
[*] Added 2nd story to hotel
[*] Updated some dialogue with small tweaks/typo fixes
[*] Added sounds to some buttons throughout the world that were missing them
[*] Fixed bug with "Summer" vocab word being stuck visible in the charms menu
[*] Fixed voice sounds not being connected to voice channel
[*] Fixed overlapping "Common Phrases" text in the Katakana District (Thank you Sonja for finding this bug!)
[*] Fixed Kanji being replaced by "美味しい" in some NPC charm windows (Thank you Sonja for finding this bug too!)
[/list]

We want to thank everyone who contributed their thoughts, feedback, and helped us track down technical issues that came up while in Early Access. We truly appreciate it all and hope you were able to enjoy your time in our game despite those issues and continue to play through it until the end credits! :3

The price will indeed be going up to $14.99, which we believe is fair considering all the time and hard work we put into making it a finished project.

If you enjoy the game, please leave a review so that the Steam algorithm can show our game to more people, and as always, if you have any technical issues, there are feedback forms accessible from the main menu OR you can leave a comment on our Steam forums. I will always try my best to get back to you as soon as I can.

Again, thank you to everyone who helped and encouraged us along the way, and to new players who were waiting for a complete game before jumping in, I hope you enjoy it!

Ok, that's it from me!

じゃあね!

notes.title: The BIG April Update
notes.content:
Hello Everyone! 

We are coming closer and closer to getting our little game to it's final form, and this update is a big step towards that goal.

[b]Features and Gameplay Updates:[/b]
[list]
[*] Added the mnemonic art from our Hiragana Reference Guide to go along with the dialogue in the Hiragana tutorial level. 
[i]This was done to improve the mnemonic visualization for complete beginners to the Japanese Language, as well as to aid the understanding of what the walls of text in our dialogue boxes are referring to.[/i]
[*] Added Game Buddy interactables to the introductory area after the tutorial to better explain what can be accessed in the menu, as well as how the game generally works.
[*] Fixed a wayward Game Buddy interactable that snuck by our radar as well.
[*] Debuffed the Emergency District Instance ever so slightly so players aren't getting TOO stuck in the bowels of... well, the Emergency District.
[*] Added 2 minigames to increase repetition to some of the areas in the vocabulary we felt needed more support.
[i]The first minigame can be found in the Emergency District to help with memorizing vocabulary regarding the Fire Department and the Police Department.[/i]
[i]The Second minigame can be found in the School District and covers the days of the week.[/i]
[*] Updated the "Charms" Map to make it more useable as a map and to improve the aesthetic for both the Main Menu and Train Station Menu.
[*] Added a new Shop NPC to the School District to give have another place to spend that Yen players have acquired by that point.
[*] And finally, Steam integration is set up on the backend, so Steam Achievements are now online! Just some basic ones at the moment, but may cook up some more over time before release.
[/list]


[b]THE BIG UPDATE:[/b]
After 2+ months of planning, hard work, and other such things, we have officially added Kanji Island to the build! This new area is accessible via the Food District after defeating the Food District Instance.
It is meant to introduce players to 52 of the most common Radicals used in around 75% of the The jōyō Kanji (Common Kanji that are taught in schools as well as the only Kanji used in Official Government Documents in Japan). This area also introduces a small side story plot and minigame themed around learning these Radicals. 

This area was a labor of love and not originally planned for this game, but we felt it was important to have something that introduced Kanji learning to players so that after they (hopefully) complete the game, they can try it again in "Kanji Mode", or at least take that knowledge with them when they start on their next phase of learning.

There are a few little things we still want to add here and there, but this was the biggest update by far. We are pleased to add it to the overall experience that this game provides and hope you find it helpful, engaging, and of course, FUN.


[b]Extra News:[/b]
We have decided on the day that we're going to be leaving Early Access and entering the "finished product" state for Kagami. After looking at what is left in our list of things to do and what timing is required for achieve those goals, it looks like it's going to be Friday May 3rd. 
This will mean a price increase for the game, so if you still want to get it a little early to provide feedback on the current state of the game or just want to get it a little cheaper and don't want to wait for a sale down the line, then I would suggest buying it before then.

After the full release, we will of course still keep our eyes on the feedback in the Steam comments, fixing any bugs that come up and the like, but we will most likely remove the dedicated feedback form accessible in the game menu and start shifting focus onto our next project.

As always, we want to thank everyone who is giving our little learning game a shot, giving us feedback to help us improve, and hope we made something memorable that also helps you learn a thing or two... or three... or more!

If you have any technical issues or constructive criticism, there are still feedback forms accessible from the main menu, OR you can leave a comment on our Steam forums. I USUALLY check both of those everyday.

I never know how to end these, so.. Thank you again and go get em' Tiger!

As for feature updates, Pop-Up Charms can now be exited from with a button press instead of having to walk away from the area.

We also updated the controls tab in the main menu with some art as supposedly showing the controller layout helps with getting Steam Deck verification (still waiting on more information on that by the way, will keep you posted). I will admit, it also does just look better now.

We are still currently hard at work on creating a bit more content that we feel is necessary for our latest Kanji update, as well as making more minigames to help with repetition of some areas of the vocabulary that we think could be improved. We hope to have the majority of these finished this month, and though I can't make any guarantees as of yet, I am optimistic considering the workflow thus far.

Thank you again to Blazzical for helping to find some of the technical issues that we initially overlooked, and as always, we welcome any feedback, weather through our feedback forms accessible on the main menu of the game or on the discussion boards here on steam.

Well, that's all from me. Happy Gaming and until next time!

notes.title: Quick Update for Dialogue Looping Issue
notes.content:
We believe we fixed all the dialogue looping NPCs in the last update we made a few days ago BUT we wanted to be sure it wouldn't happen again in case we missed one. 

The bug itself was also a really annoying thing to happen to someone if they did not save recently as the restart required would cause loss of progress, which we do recognize as being incredibly frustrating and do sincerely apologize if you were affected. 

In this update, we added an extra check in the code that should prevent any looping from being possible at all, which was inspired by one of the comments we received in these forums.

This update also has a bonus effect of not bringing up dialogues if the NPC has a charm window open.

If you experience any issues with looping dialogue or any issues in general, please fill out a feedback form or let us know in these forums.

Thank you and happy gaming! :D

notes.title: We are releasing into Early Access TODAY!
notes.content:
おはよう / こんにちは / こんばんは !

Today after a little more than a year of development, we are releasing our little language learning game in early access! We're excited and nervous as this is technically our first official game release, but more excited than anything.

We have a link to a form in the main menu for any bugs or feedback and encourage anyone who wants to report an issue or let us know what you think use that form to do so to make it easier on us to track those things.

We hope you find it as educational, fun, engaging, and compelling as we do. We poured a lot of ourselves into this project, and hopefully that shows at least a little bit.

[b]Thank you and enjoy! :D[/b]

- Zach from Iconoclast Games
